// repo-grounded bug bounty learning system

Bug Bounty 170-Day Series

Is version me public toxictest/bug-hunting repo ke hands-on style ko aur simple banaya gaya hai. Ab har bug block ke andar Description + Reproduce / Process + Impact + Mitigation diya gaya hai, aur reproduce steps ke liye English / Hinglish toggle bhi add hai. Saath hi AI aur LLM security ke extra days add karke series ko 170 days tak le gaye hain.

170 days Days 1-16 repo-mirror multi-bug style Days 17-120 research expansion retained Days 121-160 advanced variants Authorized labs / owned apps only Days 161-170 AI / LLM security
How To Use Web Workflow Phase Map Day Cards Bug Bounty Vault Source Map Main Index

How to use this page

170 / 170 days visible
Search + phase filter + completion tracking localStorage me save hota hai. Repo-mirror days me ek day ke andar multiple bug blocks milenge. English ya Hinglish steps toggle se practice aur easy ho jayegi. Print sirf visible day cards ka clean export deta hai.
Reproduce / process ko simple toggle se dekho.
Suggested routine: ek day card kholo → har bug block ka reproduce path padho → authorized lab / owned app me verify karo → evidence save karo → mitigation note karo → completion mark karo.

Safe web workflow for reproduce blocks

StepKya karna hai
1. Scope firstSirf owned apps, official labs, ya written authorization wale targets use karo.
2. BaselineNormal request/response, role, object state, token state, and visible UI ko first capture karo.
3. One change at a timeHar test me ek hi variable change karo: role, token, object ID, host header, destination URL, ya rendering input.
4. EvidenceScreenshots, request path, response delta, headers, timestamps, and final state ko preserve karo.
5. RedactionReal secrets, third-party data, ya unrelated user data ko notes me redact karke hi store karo.
6. Write the fixHar observation ke saath expected safe behavior aur correct remediation layer bhi note karo.
Ye page learning aur authorized validation ke liye hai. Real third-party systems par bina written authorization testing mat karo.

Phase map

Repo Mirror

1-16 · Public repo day layout mirrored more faithfully, with multiple bug blocks per day where the repo had multiple files.

Auth & Session Deepening

17-30 · Identity, recovery, token, and session trust with reproduce, impact, and mitigation blocks.

Browser & Client-Side Thinking

31-45 · Rendering, framing, client trust, CORS, WebSockets, and browser evidence capture.

Access Control & API Logic

46-60 · IDOR, roles, GraphQL, API behavior, race conditions, and workflow abuse cases.

Server-Side Trust Boundaries

61-75 · SSRF, file flows, template trust, parser issues, defaults, and information disclosure.

Recon & Surface Mapping

76-90 · Scope-first recon, asset mapping, prioritization, and safe lead generation.

Reporting & Severity

91-105 · Minimal reproductions, impact writing, remediation targeting, and retest discipline.

Long-Term Practice System

106-120 · Note systems, review loops, ethics, and sustainable bug-hunting routines.

Variant Expansion & Capstones

121-160 · 40 more days of advanced variants, capstones, and modern edge cases before the new AI/LLM phase.

AI & LLM Security Awareness

161-170 · Prompt injection, unsafe output handling, sensitive AI disclosure, agent authorization, RAG access control, prompt leakage, poisoning awareness, and overreliance review.

HTTP and HTTPS available
transportday 1/Http & https both available.txt

Description

The website is not fully protected by an SSL certificate. This could allow an attacker in a Man-in-the-Middle position to obtain usernames and passwords of users visiting the site.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the domain https://abc.com
  2. Copy the URL and open an incognito tab
  3. Paste the URL and remove the "S" from the domain and check if it redirects it to http
  4. If it opens on http, it is vulnerable.

Impact

If a user were to visit this page from a public or shared network (eg, office, airport, library, etc) and login an account, a malicious user on the same network would be able to obtain that user's username and password by conducting a Man-in-the-Middle attack using Wireshark. This would allow the malicious user complete access to the user's account.

Mitigation

Check for an expired SSL certificate or implement HSTS.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Evidence: redirect chain, HSTS, cookie flags, and the final scheme after opening the same route twice.
Sources: Http & https both available.txt (repo) · abc.com
HTTP by default
transportday 1/Http by default.txt

Description

The website is not fully protected by an SSL certificate. This could allow an attacker in a Man-in-the-Middle position to obtain usernames and passwords of users visiting the site.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Open the domain - http://abc.com
  2. Copy the URL and open a new tab
  3. Paste the URL and add a "S" in the domain and check if it redirects it to https
  4. If it does not open on https, it is vulnerable.

Impact

If a user were to visit this page from a public or shared network (eg, office, airport, library, etc) and login into an account, a malicious user on the same network would be able to obtain that user's username and password by conducting a Man-in-the-Middle attack using Wireshark. This would allow the malicious user complete access to the user's account.

Mitigation

Add an SSL certificate so that the website becomes secure and opens on HTTPS.

Evidence / Notes:

  • Evidence: redirect chain, HSTS, cookie flags, and the final scheme after opening the same route twice.

Improper Cache-Control on sensitive Page
cacheday 1/Improper cache control.txt

Description

The cache-control and pragma HTTP header have not been set properly or are missing allowing the browser and proxies to cache content.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the URL
  2. Login using the desired credentials
  3. Open any sensitive page like (account / settings /profile )
  4. Click on the Logout button
  5. Press the back button of the browser
  6. User's sensitive information will be visible on the page

Impact

When sensitive data is being stored and transmitted by the application which does not have the Cache-Control header, an advanced attacker can access the sensitive data, phish users and cause reputational damage to the business.

Mitigation

Add the security headers that will prevent the site's cache to get loaded again after the session has been terminated.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Evidence: logout path, browser back-button result, and response headers on the sensitive page.
Sources: Improper cache control.txt (repo)
Reset token is invalidated after use
tokenday 1/Token is invalidated after use.txt

Description

This bug focuses on reset token is invalidated after use so you can verify the exact trust boundary the repo day is teaching.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Open the URL https://website.com
  2. Go to Forgot password page
  3. Enter email and received reset link
  4. Change the password twice or thrice using the same reset link
  5. Reset token is not expiring after re-use

Impact

The attacker can reuse the reset token of the user and update the password which would lead to an account takeover

Mitigation

All password reset tokens should automatically expire after the issuance of new ones.

Evidence / Notes:
  • This vulnerability can be checked on reset token, invite token and verification token.
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Variants: reset, invite, verification, and any one-time email links.
Sources: Token is invalidated after use.txt (repo) · website.com
Weak Password Reset Implementation
authday 1/Weak Password Reset Implementation.txt

Description

When the password reset implementation is weak, the strength of the overall authentication process for the application is diminished. Tokens sent over HTTP, predictable reset tokens, and long expiry times create weak conditions for the password reset implementation.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to forgot password page of the website
  2. Enter the registered email
  3. Go to the email inbox
  4. Right-click on the box and copy the link
  5. Paste the link in the new tab
  6. Check if the link is on HTTP HTTP LINK

Impact

This vulnerability could lead to data theft from the attackers ability to manipulate data through their access to the application, and their ability to interact with other users.

Mitigation

Enforce account-state checks on the server, require verification before privileged features, and keep identity transitions explicit and auditable.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Compare: guest, unverified, verified, recovered, and step-up protected states.
Sources: Weak Password Reset Implementation.txt (repo)
Weak Registration Implementation
authday 1/Weak Registration Implementation.txt

Description

Broken authentication and session management vulnerabilities exist when a user is able to access resources or perform actions not intended for their user role. Identity and access controls can be bypassed through a variety of ways including but not limited to, calling an internal post authentication page, modifying the given URL parameters, by manipulating the form, or by counterfeiting sessions.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Register on the website
  2. An account verification link will be sent by email
  3. Go to email inbox
  4. Right-click on the box and copy the link
  5. Paste the link in the new tab and check if it is on HTTP
  6. Hit enter and check if the account is being opened HTTP LINK

Impact

Broken authentication and session management could lead to data theft through the attackers ability to manipulate data through their access to the application, and their ability to interact with other users, including performing other malicious attacks, which would appear to originate from a legitimate user.

Mitigation

Enforce account-state checks on the server, require verification before privileged features, and keep identity transitions explicit and auditable.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Compare: guest, unverified, verified, recovered, and step-up protected states.
Sources: Weak Registration Implementation.txt (repo)

Broken link hijacking
url-trustday 2/Broken Link Hijacking.txt

Description

This bug focuses on broken link hijacking so you can verify whether the application trusts destinations, redirects, or linked resources more than it should.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Open the link https://target.example
  2. Click on the social media icons like - Twitter / Facebook / Instagram, etc
  3. If not the account will not be made, it will return - PAGE NOT FOUND or ACCOUNT NOT FOUND
  4. The attacker can create an account by the company's name.

Impact

An attacker can create an account on the social media platform with that username and impersonate the company.

Mitigation

Validate redirect destinations against strict allowlists, strip sensitive parameters from user-controlled redirects, and minimize referer exposure.

Clickjacking (Bugcrowd note)
browser-uiday 2/Clickjacking - Bugcrowd.txt

Description

Clickjacking, also known as a "UI redress attack", is when an attacker uses multiple transparent or opaque layers to trick a user into clicking on a button or link on another page when they were intending to click on the top-level page. Thus, the attacker is "hijacking" clicks meant for their page and routing them to another page, most likely owned by another application, domain, or both.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Open the target.com
  2. Copy the profile URL and paste it on the clickjacking file and save
  3. Open the clijacking file and the target.com will be vulnerable to Clickjacking and loads successfully into the iframe of the attacker.
  4. The attacker can perform a sensitive action

Impact

Using a similar technique, keystrokes can also be hijacked. With a carefully crafted combination of stylesheets, iframes, and text boxes, a user can be led to believe they are typing in the password to their email or bank account, but are instead typing into an invisible frame controlled by the attacker.

Mitigation

Use frame protection, clear confirmation UX, and browser-security headers that stop sensitive actions from being silently reframed.

Evidence / Notes:
  • For bugcrowd, it will be only accepted on features like: 1 - Delete account without password through clickjacking 2 - 2FA enable/disable without password through clickjacking
  • Evidence: framing behavior, response headers, and the exact sensitive action exposed.
Sources: Clickjacking - Bugcrowd.txt (repo)

DMARC record not found
email-securityday 2/DMARC.txt

Description

DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) is an email authentication protocol. It is designed to give email domain owners the ability to protect their domain from unauthorized use, commonly known as email spoofing.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Visit - https://target.example
  2. Enter the domain name - target.com and hit go
  3. The domain name will show No DMARC Record found

Impact

Spammers can forge the "From" address on email messages to make messages appear to come from someone in your domain. If spammers use your domain to send spam or junk email, your domain quality is negatively affected. People who get the forged emails can mark them as spam or junk, which can impact authentic messages sent from your domain.

Mitigation

Implement the DMARC Record which will prevent the attacker to spoof the email domains.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Focus: DMARC record not found
  • Preserve the smallest reproducible proof with clear scope.
Sources: DMARC.txt (repo) · mxtoolbox.com
Delete account without a password
reauthday 2/Delete account without password.txt

Description

The removal of an account is one of the sensitive parts of a web application that needs to protect, therefore removing an account should validate the authenticity of the user, however, I have found that when removing an account, the system did not require the user to input the account password.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the website and login into your account.
  2. Visit the profile/settings section.
  3. A delete/cancel/deactivate/remove account button will be displayed.
  4. Press that button and the account will be successfully deleted.

Impact

The target doesn't verify the request with a Valid OTP or password before triggering Right to Access/Deletion & allows an attacker to delete User Accounts without user interaction.

Mitigation

Put reauthentication when anyone/user is deleting an account, and ask the user to input a password before the completion of the account deletion.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Good surfaces: delete account, change email, change password, payout, and other destructive actions.
Sources: Delete account without password.txt (repo)

Exif Geo Location - Automatic user enumeration
metadataDay 3/Exif geo location - Automatic user enumeration.txt

Description

When a user downloads an image in example.com, the uploaded image’s EXIF Geolocation Data does not get stripped. As a result, anyone can get sensitive information of example.com users like their Geo-location, their Device information like Device Name, Version, Software & Software version used, etc.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to https://target.example
  2. Download an image present on the website
  3. Go to https://target.example
  4. Upload the downloaded image
  5. Exif data will be visible

Impact

The user's private data has not been stripped and is being shown publically which is a strong privacy concern.

Mitigation

Strip nonessential metadata before publishing or downloading user content and avoid exposing sensitive local or environment details.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Artifacts: EXIF, document properties, clipboard content, or local-environment data revealed by the feature.
Sources: Exif geo location - Automatic user enumeration.txt (repo) · www.canva.cn · jimpl.com

Broken authentication and session management-failure to invalidate session on logout (client-side/server-side)
sessionDay 3/Failure to Invalidate session - on logout - Client side Server side - Without Burp.txt

Description

This application fails to invalidate a user’s session on logout, leaving the account vulnerable to session hijacking. An attacker may compromise a user’s session then be able to change the password of the account and lock out the legitimate user.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the URL - https://target.example
  2. Open the same account on two different tabs on the same browser - Broswer A
  3. Click on the Logout from one tab - TAB A
  4. Once the session is terminated, go to the second tab (TAB B) and update some data and save it
  5. Post changing the data, click on the refresh button.
  6. Once refreshed, your second tab session is also terminated.
  7. Login again to the same account and the data has been changed

Impact

This vulnerability can lead to reputational damage and indirect financial loss to the company as customers may view the application as insecure.

Mitigation

Rotate or revoke sessions after logout and sensitive changes, invalidate stale cookies server-side, and keep state consistent across devices and tabs.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Compare old tab, second browser, and post-password-change session state.
Sources: Failure to Invalidate session - on logout - Client side Server side - Without Burp.txt (repo) · www.target.com

Harden SPF and DMARC alignment, send trustworthy account notifications, and align email-based trust with actual application security controls.

Origin IP disclosure leads to WAF Bypass
source-exposureDay 3/Origin IP - WAF bypass.txt

Description

By using these IP address as a resolver instead of the intended addresses I'm able to access the service without going through the WAF, thus I'm able to forward unfiltered payloads to the service, as well as avoiding the common protections offered by Cloudflare, also being able to perform crippling denial-of-service towards the origin.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Enumerate the subdomains of https://target.com
  2. Check the firewall used by the tool DNSlytics or WafW00f
  3. To get origin IP - Use sites like : https://target.example , https://target.example
  4. Do a IP lookup of the IP
  5. Enter the IP on the URL and hit enter to check if the IP loads the subdomain name

Impact

Cloudflare bypasses can have a significant impact, as any adversary is now able to communicate with the origin server directly, enabling them to perform unfiltered attacks (such as denial-of-service), and data retrieval Shodan - ssl.cert.subject.CN:"domain.com"+200

Mitigation

Remove secrets from shipped assets, restrict public diagnostics and source maps, and keep client config intentionally minimal.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo references or example reports are linked below for extra reading.
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Artifacts: client bundles, debug routes, maps, public files, and redacted screenshots.
Sources: Origin IP - WAF bypass.txt (repo) · target.com · search.censys.io · www.shodan.io
Reset token leaked in response
tokenDay 3/Token leaked in response.txt

Description

I have found that if user open the link of reset password and than click on any external links within the reset password page its leak password reset token in response.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Open this link https://target.example
  2. Create an accout and enter your email on forgot password page
  3. Intercept the request in burpsuite and send it to repeater

Scope tokens tightly, expire them quickly, rotate them on re-issue, bind them to the intended action, and reject reuse server-side.

No rate limit on Change email leads to email triggering
reauthDay 4/Change email rate limit.txt

Description

Rate limiting is a strategy for limiting network traffic. It puts a cap on how often someone can repeat an action within a certain timeframe – for instance, trying to log in to an account.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Open this link https://abc.com
  2. Go to settings and enter new email address and, the password, if asked.
  3. Intercept the request in burpsuite
  4. Send the request to intruder and click on clear
  5. Use null payloads as payload type and enter 100 as payload count.
  6. Click on start attack and multiple emails will be received on the new email address's emailbox.

Impact

If the company is using any email service software API or some tool that has been bought for the emails being sent on the support domain, the rate limit can result in financial loss and it can also slow down your services as huge/mass mails will lead to disruption of data that original user might send or the quota that has been bought might be exhausted.

Mitigation

1 - IP Based Blocking 2 - Captcha 3 - Firewall 4 - Reducing the number of API requests

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Good surfaces: delete account, change email, change password, payout, and other destructive actions.
Sources: Change email rate limit.txt (repo) · abc.com

Account lockout bypass by manipulating networks
rate-limitDay 5/Account lockout bypass.txt

Description

This bug focuses on account lockout bypass by manipulating networks so you can verify the exact trust boundary the repo day is teaching.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Open the website / APK
  2. Now enter the email id and wrong password here many times.
  3. Now here the account is locked.
  4. If you are try to login than application is pop up a message (Your account is temporarily locked. Please try again later).
  5. So here all the attacker has to do is change the network.
  6. Enter the correct credentials and the account is successful logged in by bypassing the account lockout mechanism.

An attacker will be able to brute force the password by manipulating the networks and takeover the account

Apply server-side throttling, cooldowns, account and IP protections, queue controls, and abuse logging consistently across related endpoints.

No password policy
authDay 5/No passsword policy.txt

Description

Some websites prevent the users to use passwords constructed of character combinations that otherwise meet company policy, but should no longer be used because they have been deemed insecure for one or more reasons, such as being easily guessed, following a common pattern, or public disclosure from previous data breaches. Common examples are 1234, qwerty, or the word password itself.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to https://abc.com/signup.
  2. Create an account by typing your email address and password to "1"
  3. Hit the "Sign Up for web" button.
  4. The account will be created.

Impact

Since the site is accepting single digit password, it will be easily guessable and bruteforceable leading to account takeover

Mitigation

Some policies suggest or impose requirements on what type of password a user can choose, such as: the use of both upper-case and lower-case letters (case sensitivity) inclusion of one or more numerical digits inclusion of special characters, such as @, #, $ prohibition of words found in a password blacklist prohibition of words found in the user's personal information prohibition of the use of company name or an abbreviation prohibition of passwords that match the format of calendar dates, license plate numbers, telephone numbers, or other common numbers

Evidence / Notes:
  • Can be checked on registration and change password option
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Compare: guest, unverified, verified, recovered, and step-up protected states.
Sources: No passsword policy.txt (repo) · abc.com
Open Redirect GET Based
url-trustDay 5/Open redirect get based.txt

Description

Open redirect is a security flaw in an app or a web page that causes it to fail to properly authenticate URLs. Web users often encounter redirection when they visit the Web site of a company whose name has been changed or which has been acquired by another company.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Visit the link https://target.example
  2. Put the payload/website name as //evil.com after the parameter
  3. It should appear like - https://target.example
  4. Enter the email id and password
  5. Click on sign in and the page will be redirected

Impact

An attacker can use this vulnerability to redirect users to other malicious websites, which can be used for phishing and similar attacks The attacker can redirect it to evil.com and other malicious websites like https://target.example

Mitigation

Validate redirect destinations against strict allowlists, strip sensitive parameters from user-controlled redirects, and minimize referer exposure.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo references or example reports are linked below for extra reading.
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Artifacts: starting URL, final destination, referer or token leakage, and allowlist behavior.

Sensitive token via URL
tokenDay 5/Sensitive token in URL.txt

Description

Sensitive data can be exposed when it is not behind an authorization barrier. When this information is exposed it can place the application at further risk of compromise. Method 1- Sensitive data can be exposed when it is not behind an authorization barrier. When this information is exposed it can place the application at further risk of compromise.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to https://target.example
  2. Login into your Account
  3. The email/username and the password will be visible in plaintext in the URL
  4. Go to https://target.example
  5. Login into your Account
  6. Change your password ( from inside the account or using reset link)
  7. Password changed and now see the link (old and new password will be shown in URL)

Impact

This vulnerability can lead to data theft through the attacker’s ability to manipulate data through their access to the application, and their ability to interact with other users, including performing other malicious attacks, which would appear to originate from a legitimate user. Method 2 - Even after Logout, if any person has access to your system or if you are using a public system - that person can have access to your password through browser history. ( Password will be shown in browser history). it can easily lead to an account takeover.

Mitigation

Scope tokens tightly, expire them quickly, rotate them on re-issue, bind them to the intended action, and reject reuse server-side.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Variants: reset, invite, verification, and any one-time email links.
Sources: Sensitive token in URL.txt (repo) · www.abc.com
Token leakage via referrer - 3rd Party
tokenDay 5/Token Leakage via referer third party(1).txt

Description

The Referer HTTP request header is used to show the URL of the page a user requested the resource from. This application’s Referer headers leak valid user tokens over an untrusted third-party link.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to target.com
  2. Visit the forgot password page
  3. Enter the email for which the password has to be reset
  4. Open the Password reset link received from the email
  5. Intercept the request (I have used burp suite)
  6. Click on any link which is 3rd party
  7. You can see the link for reset password in the referrer

Impact

Token Leakage via Referer header can lead to indirect financial loss through an attacker accessing, deleting, or modifying data from within the application, providing that they can escalate privileges and execute API calls.

Mitigation

Scope tokens tightly, expire them quickly, rotate them on re-issue, bind them to the intended action, and reject reuse server-side.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Host like facebook, snapchat, instagram, twitter, google will be considered as trusted third party - P5
  • Variants: reset, invite, verification, and any one-time email links.
Sources: Token Leakage via referer third party(1).txt (repo)

metadataDay 6/Clipboard enabled.txt

Description

This bug focuses on clipboard enabled so you can verify the exact trust boundary the repo day is teaching.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Install an application Start the application. Enter text into input fields that ask for sensitive data. Try copying this data into a note application. If strings can be copied and pasted, the clipboard is enabled. For Android, the Drozer module post.capture.clipboard can be used to extract data from the clipboard:dz> run post.capture.clipboard

Impact

In enabled clipboard increases the risk of the exposure of sensitive information. If data such as credit card numbers, social security numbers, or other sensitive information is cut and paste from or into the application, it may be saved to the phone and accessed at a later date.

Mitigation

Strip nonessential metadata before publishing or downloading user content and avoid exposing sensitive local or environment details.

Session Hijacking - Local Attack Vector
sessionDay 6/Session Hijacking.txt

Description

Session Hijacking is an attack that permits an attacker to hijack a valid user session. The attack explores a limitation in the way the web application manages the session ID, more specifically the vulnerable web application.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Open browser and download cookie editor
  2. Login into account
  3. Now goto cookie editor addon and click export all cookies.
  4. Log out from your account
  5. Now go to the login page and just simply go to cookie editor addon and click import a cookie and paste the code which we previously exported.
  6. After pasting just refresh the page and that's done you are now logged into your account without login details.

Impact

A successful session hijacking attack gives the attacker access to the victim's account. This could mean access to higher level privileges or the ability to look at sensitive data.

Mitigation

Rotate or revoke sessions after logout and sensitive changes, invalidate stale cookies server-side, and keep state consistent across devices and tabs.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Compare old tab, second browser, and post-password-change session state.
Sources: Session Hijacking.txt (repo)

Cross site request forgery (CSRF)
csrfDay 7/CSRF.txt

Description

Cross site request forgery (CSRF), also known as XSRF, is an attack vector that tricks a web browser into executing an unwanted action in an application to which a user is logged in.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Open https://abc.com/profile
  2. Update the full profile & take that request in burp.
  3. Go to engagement tools & click on make CSRF POC.
  4. Click on test in browser and copy the request
  5. Open a new browser or an incognito mode (proxy enabled) with the victim account logged in and submit the request
  6. The victim profile will get successfully updated.

Impact

A successful CSRF attack can be devastating for both the business and user. It can result in damaged client relationships, unauthorized fund transfers, changed passwords and data theft—including stolen session cookies.

Mitigation

Use anti-CSRF tokens, same-site cookies, origin validation, and re-auth or confirmation where the action is sensitive.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo references or example reports are linked below for extra reading.
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Capture the missing token/origin control and the final state change.
Sources: CSRF.txt (repo) · abc.com

Blind XSS
xssDay 8/Blind XSS.txt

Description

Blind XSS vulnerabilities are a variant of persistent XSS vulnerabilities. They occur when the attacker input is saved by the web server and executed as a malicious script in another part of the application or in another application.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Use only an official lab or owned application with a harmless test marker.
  2. Trace how the value moves from input to reflection, storage, preview, or downstream viewer.
  3. Identify the rendering context and which user or role would see it.
  4. Preserve the smallest proof of unsafe rendering without using a risky live payload here.

Impact

Unsafe rendering can expose sessions, trusted user actions, internal panels, or downstream viewers to attacker-controlled content.

Mitigation

Apply context-aware output encoding, safe templating, sanitizer policy where needed, and defense-in-depth controls such as CSP.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo references or example reports are linked below for extra reading.
  • High-risk payload details were intentionally normalized here; use only official labs or owned apps for deeper validation.

Weak Captcha Implementation
rate-limitDay 10/Captcha implementation vulnerability - method 1 - Copy.txt

Description

CAPTCHA (“Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart”) is a type of challenge-response test used by many web applications to ensure that the response is not generated by a computer. CAPTCHA implementations are often vulnerable to various kinds of attacks even if the generated CAPTCHA is unbreakable. This section will help you to identify these kinds of attacks.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the target
  2. Fill the form with the captcha
  3. Take the data on burpsuite
  4. Send the data to the intruder
  5. Apply null payloads ( I applied 100 ) and set the threads
  6. Start attack
  7. Requests will be successfully submitted

Impact

The captcha is being bypassed as the captcha is normally implemented once/request but I am generating 100 requests on the same captcha.

Mitigation

Apply server-side throttling, cooldowns, account and IP protections, queue controls, and abuse logging consistently across related endpoints.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Measure request count, timing window, and whether related endpoints share the same guardrails.
Sources: Captcha implementation vulnerability - method 1 - Copy.txt (repo)

Host Header Poisoning/Injection
host-headerDay 10/Host Header Injection.txt

Description

A Host header attack, also known as Host header injection, is a web attack where the attacker provides a false Host header to the web application

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the Forgot password
  2. Enter the email
  3. Take the data on burpsuite
  4. Send it to the repeater
  5. Change the host to bing.com (Can also try X-Forwarded-host)
  6. Click go and check the response code
  7. If it comes as 200 OK, check the mail.
  8. If the token comes with bing.com (attacker's domain) it will be considered as vulnerable.

Impact

If the server implicitly trusts the Host header, and fails to validate or escape it properly, an attacker may be able to use this input to inject harmful payloads that manipulate server-side behavior.

Mitigation

Use a trusted server-side canonical host configuration and never build security-sensitive URLs from unvalidated client headers.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo references or example reports are linked below for extra reading.
  • Check both Host and forwarded-host style headers when testing reset flows or absolute URLs.
Sources: Host Header Injection.txt (repo)
Missing Secure or HTTP only
transportDay 10/Missing Secure or HTTP only - from Session Cookie.txt

Description

This cookie does not have the Secure flag set. When a cookie is set with the Secure flag, it instructs the browser that the cookie can only be accessed over secure SSL channels. This is an important security protection for session cookies.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to target.com
  2. Go to cookie editor
  3. Export the cookie
  4. Paste it in notepad
  5. Check for the session keyword
  6. Check if the Secure/HTTP only is missing

Impact

The secure flag should be set on all cookies that are used for transmitting sensitive data when accessing content over HTTPS. If cookies are used to transmit session tokens, then areas of the application that are accessed over HTTPS should employ their own session handling mechanism, and the session tokens used should never be transmitted over unencrypted communications.

Mitigation

Force HTTPS on every entry point, deploy valid certificates, add HSTS where appropriate, and ensure secure cookies never ride on downgraded routes.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Do check which cookie is carrying session then proceed!
  • Evidence: redirect chain, HSTS, cookie flags, and the final scheme after opening the same route twice.
Sources: Missing Secure or HTTP only - from Session Cookie.txt (repo)

Application level DOS
rate-limitDay 11/App Level DOS - Long Password or String.txt

Description

It is often confused with network level DoS. This vulnerability occurs because faulty implementation of some functions on the application. The entry point for this vulnerability involves interaction with application and these kind of attacks are often tough to identify and sometimes even tougher to prevent.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to a target.com
  2. Enter a long string of numeric / alphanumeric digits on any input field ( like - fname, lname, pass, etc.)
  3. Click on save and wait for the site to respond
  4. The website starts to load and after a while, it returns a 500 error
  5. Open the site with a different IP and system and check if the site is responding.
  6. The site won't open as the long digits has lead to app level DOS

Impact

Application Layer Denial of service will have the same effect as network level DoS . It can take down the application server or make application unavailable to use for other users. Fix - Proper Input validation can help to mitigate this vulnerability.

Mitigation

Apply server-side throttling, cooldowns, account and IP protections, queue controls, and abuse logging consistently across related endpoints.

Evidence / Notes:

OAuth Misconfiguration Account Takeover using CSRF
authDay 11/OAuth Misconfig Account Takeover - CSRF.txt

Description

A Cross Site Request Forgery attack involves a bad guy tricking a user into clicking on a link that changes some state on the target system. If the user is already authenticated with the target system he might not even notice the attack since the browser will send authentication headers or cookies automatically.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to https://target.example
  2. If the application supports OAuth functionality service providers like Facebook and Gmail which you can link your social accounts to the application https://target.example
  3. Intercept the request using Burpsuite and now click on Facebook / Gmail icon for linking of social account to the account
  4. Observe the request and lookout whether state parameter is implemented or not
  5. If state parameter is not there which means it can be vulnerable to CSRF attack
  6. Once you are successfully authenticated then intercept the callback request from Facebook looks like below GET /auth/facebook/callback?code=XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX HTTP/1.1 Host: abc.com
  7. Generate a CSRF poc on this page and save it as poc.html
  8. Now create another account an victim's account on https://target.example then go to the setting page where you can link the social account.
  9. Now open poc.html page in the browser and click on submit button
  10. Facebook account is successfully linked with victim account on https://target.example
  11. Logout from the application and try to login from your social account
  12. Successfully logged into the victim account of https://target.example

Impact

Broken identity gates can grant access, verification state, or recovery power before the server has enough proof to trust the user.

Mitigation

Enforce account-state checks on the server, require verification before privileged features, and keep identity transitions explicit and auditable.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo file includes extra URLs or examples linked in the sources area.
  • Compare: guest, unverified, verified, recovered, and step-up protected states.
Sources: OAuth Misconfig Account Takeover - CSRF.txt (repo) · www.abc.com · www.abc.com

Reproduce / Process

  2. Change Email address to victim's email address. ( victim has not received verification email)

Horizontal Privilege Escalation
access-controlDay 12/Horizontal Privilege Escalation.txt

Description

Horizontal privilege escalation can allow an attacker to gain access to data that may not necessarily belong to him. In poorly designed applications, an attacker may have the capability of identifying flaws within a Web application that allows him access to other users' information.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Create two accounts
  2. Open it on two browsers ( Firefox and Incognito Firefox)
  3. Go to account A and go to my account
  4. Click on users
  5. Go to a user and right-click on settings of the user
  6. Copy GUID (USER ID) of the user
  7. Go to account B and go to my account
  8. Click on users
  9. Go to a user and click on settings
  10. Click on reset password and capture the request
  11. Go to burp and replace the copied GUID
  12. Send it to the repeater and click on GO
  13. The password of the user of the account B will be shown in response.

Impact

An attacker can exploit horizontal escalation vulnerabilities to gain access to another user’s data, you are betraying your users’ trust, which can have reputational, legal, and financial implications.

Mitigation

Enforce object ownership and role checks on every backend action instead of assuming the UI constrained the request.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo references or example reports are linked below for extra reading.
  • Use two accounts or two roles and preserve the object ID that should have been rejected.
Sources: Horizontal Privilege Escalation.txt (repo)
Insecure direct object references (IDOR)
access-controlDay 12/IDOR.txt

Description

This can occur when a web application or application programming interface uses an identifier for direct access to an object in an internal database but does not check for access control or authentication.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Create two accounts
  2. Open it on two browsers ( Firefox and Incognito Firefox)
  3. Login into [test-email] and go to my account
  4. Click on phone number
  5. Enter phone number and capture the data on burp
  6. Copy the USER ID from the account of [test-email]
  7. Login into [test-email] and go to my account
  8. Click on phone number
  9. Enter phone number and capture the data on burp
  10. Replace the copied USER ID and forward the data
  11. The phone number of victim account will be changed.

Impact

The impact of an insecure direct object reference vulnerability depends very much on the application's functionality. Therefore, a clear list can not be easily given. Generally speaking, an IDOR vulnerability can introduce a risk for CIA (confidentiality, integrity, availability) of data.

Mitigation

Enforce object ownership and role checks on every backend action instead of assuming the UI constrained the request.

Evidence / Notes:
  • The account is getting logged in using phone number so here number plays a vital role!
  • Repo references or example reports are linked below for extra reading.
  • Use two accounts or two roles and preserve the object ID that should have been rejected.
Sources: IDOR.txt (repo)

Authentication bypass using response manipulation
authDay 13/Authentication Bypass Response Manipulation.txt

Description

This refers to an attacker gaining access equivalent to an authenticated user without ever going through an authentication procedure. This is usually the result of the attacker using an unexpected access procedure that does not go through the proper checkpoints where authentication should occur.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Visit the login page
  2. Enter the user id on the login page
  3. Go to the forget password page and enter the user's email address
  4. It will redirect you to the OTP page
  5. Enter the wrong OTP and capture the request on burp
  6. Right-click --> Do Intercept - Response to this request
  7. Change the response status from false to true and from error to success
  8. Forward the request and close the intercept.
  9. It will redirect you to the New password page.
  10. The Attacker will be able to change the victim's password now.

Impact

The attacker is able to change the victim's password just by manipulating the response which leads to full ATO of the victim.

Mitigation

Enforce account-state checks on the server, require verification before privileged features, and keep identity transitions explicit and auditable.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo references or example reports are linked below for extra reading.
  • Compare: guest, unverified, verified, recovered, and step-up protected states.
Sources: Authentication Bypass Response Manipulation.txt (repo)

ssrfDay 14/SSRF.txt

Description

Server-side request forgery (also known as SSRF) is a web security vulnerability that allows an attacker to induce the server-side application to make requests to an unintended location.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Identify a server-side fetcher such as URL preview, webhook, import, or callback field.
  2. Use a controlled callback destination instead of a third-party internal target.
  3. Submit only safe test URLs and verify whether the server makes the outbound request.

Impact

The vulnerability allows an attacker to make arbitrary HTTP/HTTPS requests inside a Ringcentral instance's network.

Mitigation

Allowlist destinations, block internal address ranges, validate redirects carefully, and isolate outbound fetchers from sensitive networks.

Disable external entities, external DTD resolution, and unsafe parser features; validate XML inputs against the exact required format.

Local File Inclusion
business-logicDay 15/local file inclusion (LFI).txt

Description

LFI stands for Local File Includes - it’s a file local inclusion vulnerability that allows an attacker to include files that exist on the target web server. Typically this is exploited by abusing dynamic file inclusion mechanisms that don’t sanitize user input. Scripts that take filenames as parameters without sanitizing the user input are good candidates for LFI vulnerabilities, a good example would be the following PHP script foo.php?file=image.jpg which takes image.jpg as a parameter. An attacker would simply replace image.jpg and insert a payload. Normally a directory traversal payload is used that escapes the script directory and traverses the filesystem directory structure, exposing sensitive files such as foo.php?file=../../../../../../../etc/passwd or sensitive files within the web application itself. Exposing sensitive information or configuration files containing SQL usernames and passwords.

Reproduce / Process

  1. Capture the normal baseline first.
  2. Use only an authorized lab or owned target.
  3. Change one variable at a time and compare the server behavior.
  4. Preserve the smallest reproducible proof.

Impact

Workflow-rule failures can produce unauthorized actions, state desynchronization, or business-impacting abuse.

Mitigation

Model the workflow server-side, validate every state transition, and retest adjacent paths whenever a business rule is fixed.

Evidence / Notes:
  • Repo references or example reports are linked below for extra reading.
  • Focus: Local File Inclusion
  • Preserve the smallest reproducible proof with clear scope.
Sources: local file inclusion (LFI).txt (repo)
Repo resources / helper files: LFI Reports.txt

Login state map
auth

Description

This bug focuses on login state map so you can verify whether This day is about identity gates and whether the application grants trust too early, to the wrong user state, or without enough proof. Create a clean state diagram for guest, failed-login, locked, MFA-pending, and authenticated users..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the URL https://target.com and open the login, signup, verification, or recovery flow for your test account.
  2. Complete the flow once normally so you know the expected behavior.
  3. Repeat the same flow and change only one trust condition like unverified state, second account, callback value, or token order.
  4. Submit the request and compare whether the server still grants access or state change.
  5. If the application trusts the changed state too early, save the exact step, request, and final account result.

Impact

Broken identity gates can grant access, verification state, or recovery power before the server has enough proof to trust the user.

Mitigation

Enforce account-state checks on the server, require verification before privileged features, and keep identity transitions explicit and auditable.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Compare: guest vs unverified vs verified vs recovered
  • Evidence: session issuance, state change, protected route access
Sources: OWASP Authentication · PortSwigger Authentication

Password reset completion flow
session

Description

This bug focuses on password reset completion flow so you can verify whether This day is about whether a session remains valid, transferable, or insufficiently rotated after a sensitive identity event. After reset, inspect session rotation, device revocation, and security notifications..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the URL https://target.com and login using the same account in Browser A and Browser B.
  2. In Browser A, logout or change the password from the settings page.
  3. Move to Browser B and open any sensitive page like profile, settings, or dashboard.
  4. Change some account data and click save, or try to reload the protected page.
  5. If Browser B still works as logged-in after the trust change, save both browser states and the final response.

Impact

If old sessions remain valid after sensitive events, attackers or unintended holders of stale cookies can keep access they should have lost.

Mitigation

Rotate or revoke sessions after logout and sensitive changes, invalidate stale cookies server-side, and keep state consistent across devices and tabs.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Compare old tab, second browser, captured request
  • Evidence: before/after cookies, device state, logout path
Sources: OWASP Session Management · OWASP Forgot Password

Change-email protections
reauth

Description

This bug focuses on change-email protections so you can verify whether This day is about step-up verification: the application should demand fresh proof before destructive or identity-changing actions. Sensitive identity changes should demand fresh proof, safe rollback, and user alerts..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the URL https://target.com and login using the desired credentials.
  2. Open the account settings page and choose a sensitive action like change email, change password, payout, or delete account.
  3. Try to complete the action without entering the current password or another fresh verification step.
  4. Submit the action and reload the account settings page.
  5. If the sensitive change is completed without re-authentication, save the request and final account state.

Impact

Without fresh proof on destructive or identity-changing actions, an existing browser state can be abused to alter ownership-critical settings.

Mitigation

Require fresh credentials or step-up verification for destructive or identity-changing actions and confirm them with server-side checks.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Good actions: change email, change password, payout, delete account
  • Evidence: request accepted without fresh proof
Sources: OWASP Authentication · OWASP Session Management

  5. If Browser B still works as logged-in after the trust change, save both browser states and the final response.

Impact

If old sessions remain valid after sensitive events, attackers or unintended holders of stale cookies can keep access they should have lost.

Mitigation

Rotate or revoke sessions after logout and sensitive changes, invalidate stale cookies server-side, and keep state consistent across devices and tabs.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Compare old tab, second browser, captured request
  • Evidence: before/after cookies, device state, logout path
Sources: OWASP Session Management · OWASP Forgot Password

Description

  • Check every related endpoint, not only the visible form

browser-ui

Description

This bug focuses on devtools-first investigation workflow so you can verify whether This day is about browser-mediated trust: framing, visual cues, script policy, network inspection, and what the user is tricked into doing or seeing. Turn browser tabs, forms, and requests into a repeatable testing notebook..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the URL https://target.com and login using the desired credentials.
  2. Open the feature you want to test such as profile, settings, search, upload, or checkout.
  3. Use DevTools Network tab to capture the exact request, response, headers, cookies, and redirect chain.
  4. Replay the same action once more and change only one value like object ID, token, role, or URL parameter.
  5. If the server behavior changes in an unsafe way, save the request pair and use that as your reproduce block.

Impact

Browser-side trust failures can trick users into approving actions they never intended to perform.

Mitigation

Use frame protection, clear confirmation UX, and browser-security headers that stop sensitive actions from being silently reframed.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Headers: frame-ancestors and X-Frame-Options
  • Surfaces: profile, wallet, payout, admin actions
Sources: Chrome DevTools Network · PortSwigger Clickjacking

IDOR basics with object ownership
access-control

Description

This bug focuses on idor basics with object ownership so you can verify whether This day is about the missing or weak server-side checks that should bind a user, role, or object to a permitted action. Objects should belong to users or roles explicitly; test for missing ownership checks..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Create two test accounts and login to them in two separate browsers.
  2. Using Account A, open the target feature and capture the request that updates or reads the object.
  3. Copy the object ID or account-linked value from Account A.
  4. Using Account B, replay the same request while replacing its object value with Account A data.
  5. If Account B can read or modify Account A data, save both account states, the changed object ID, and the response.

Impact

Broken access control threatens confidentiality, integrity, and privilege boundaries across users, roles, and objects.

Mitigation

Enforce object ownership and role checks on every backend action instead of assuming the UI constrained the request.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Use two accounts or two roles
  • Focus on ownership-changing actions and admin-only surfaces
Sources: PortSwigger Access Control · OWASP WSTG

Admin panel vs API parity
api

Description

This bug focuses on admin panel vs api parity so you can verify whether This day is about API-specific trust and whether direct endpoints behave more loosely than the visible UI suggests. Sometimes UI blocks an action that direct API calls still allow; compare both views..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the URL https://target.com and login using the desired credentials.
  2. Open the feature that calls the API and capture the request in DevTools or Burp.
  3. Send the request to Repeater and change only one value like role, object ID, method, or hidden field.
  4. Forward the modified request and compare the API response with what the UI allows.
  5. If the API performs more than the UI should permit, save the endpoint, modified request, and response.

Impact

API-only trust gaps can expose actions and data paths that the visible UI appears to protect.

Mitigation

Align API authorization with business rules, validate object ownership server-side, and keep endpoint exposure consistent with UI permissions.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Compare UI-limited fields with direct endpoint behavior
  • Artifacts: endpoint path, object ID, auth context
Sources: PortSwigger API Testing · OWASP API Security

GraphQL authorization thinking
graphql

Description

This bug focuses on graphql authorization thinking so you can verify whether This day is about schema-shaped access control, nested object exposure, and GraphQL-specific resource concerns. Nested fields and object graphs can hide access-control mistakes in otherwise tidy schemas..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the URL https://target.com and login using a low-privileged test account.
  2. Open the feature that sends GraphQL requests and capture the /graphql request in DevTools or Burp.
  3. Repeat the same request and change only the field list, object ID, nested object, or batch shape.
  4. Send the modified request and compare the response with what the low-privileged user should be able to access.
  5. If extra data, actions, or hidden schema details are returned, save the query, response, and affected role boundary.

Impact

Resolver or schema mistakes can leak hidden fields, bypass object controls, or multiply attack surface through a single endpoint.

Mitigation

Restrict schema exposure where appropriate, enforce authz per resolver, and cap batching, depth, and complexity for risky operations.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Watch introspection, nested fields, batching, mutation scope
  • Artifacts: query shape and unauthorized field
Sources: PortSwigger GraphQL · OWASP GraphQL

Business-logic approvals and state transitions
business-logic

Description

This bug focuses on business-logic approvals and state transitions so you can verify whether This day is about workflow mistakes that arise when product rules, not just technical rules, are enforced inconsistently. Look for approve/reject/cancel/refund style actions that move records across trust states..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the feature like checkout, coupon, invite, approval, wallet, or subscription flow.
  2. Complete the process once normally so you know the valid order of steps.
  3. Repeat the same flow and change only one business condition like order, quantity, balance, approval state, or reuse of a one-time action.
  4. Submit the action and compare the final state with what the business rule should allow.
  5. If the server accepts an invalid state or duplicate benefit, save the full step order and final result.

Impact

Workflow-rule failures can produce unauthorized actions, state desynchronization, or business-impacting abuse.

Mitigation

Model the workflow server-side, validate every state transition, and retest adjacent paths whenever a business rule is fixed.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Focus: Business-logic approvals and state transitions
  • Preserve the smallest reproducible proof with clear scope.
Sources: PortSwigger Business Logic · PortSwigger Race Conditions

Race conditions in multi-step workflows
race

Description

This bug focuses on race conditions in multi-step workflows so you can verify whether This day is about temporary sub-states and concurrent request timing that can produce unintended outcomes. Temporary sub-states can create a small but meaningful logic window..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the one-time action like coupon apply, email change confirm, reset complete, or another limited workflow.
  2. Complete it once normally to know the expected final state.
  3. Repeat the same action from two tabs or two captured requests at nearly the same time in your authorized test setup.
  4. Refresh the account or object state after both requests complete.
  5. If the application accepts both requests when only one should succeed, save both requests and the inconsistent final state.

Impact

Broken concurrency control can let repeated requests bypass one-time rules, limits, balances, or approval sequences.

Mitigation

Enforce atomic state transitions server-side, use idempotency controls, and serialize sensitive updates that should only happen once.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Artifacts: request count, timing, final inconsistent state
  • Choose one-time actions and counters
Sources: PortSwigger Race Conditions · PortSwigger All Labs

Webhook and callback trust
ssrf

Description

This bug focuses on webhook and callback trust so you can verify whether This day is about server-side outbound behavior and whether user input can influence trusted fetches or destinations. Outbound features extend the trust boundary beyond the UI; map validation expectations..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the URL field, webhook, image fetch, callback, preview, or import feature of your owned app or authorized lab.
  2. Generate a controlled callback URL that belongs to you and note the normal server behavior.
  3. Submit that URL in the target field and capture the related request.
  4. Check whether the application server makes an outbound request to your controlled destination.
  5. If the server fetches unintended destinations or trusts redirects unsafely, save the field name, request, and callback evidence.

Impact

Server-side request trust can expose internal services, metadata paths, or privileged integrations that users should never reach directly.

Mitigation

Allowlist destinations, block internal address ranges, validate redirects carefully, and isolate outbound fetchers from sensitive networks.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Common surfaces: webhooks, importers, previews, avatar fetchers
  • Use controlled listeners only
Sources: PortSwigger SSRF · OWASP SSRF

Host header and absolute-URL generation
host-header

Description

This bug focuses on host header and absolute-url generation so you can verify whether This day is about proxy and header trust, especially when applications generate absolute URLs or route logic from client-controlled values. Applications that generate links from headers can misplace trust..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the forgot-password or email-link generation flow.
  2. Enter your own test email and capture the request in Burp Suite or another proxy.
  3. Send the request to Repeater and change only the Host or forwarded-host related header.
  4. Forward the request and check the generated reset or verification link delivered to your mailbox.
  5. If the application builds the link from your supplied host value, save the request and resulting email.

Impact

Trusted host metadata can poison reset links, routing decisions, and other absolute-URL workflows.

Mitigation

Use a trusted server-side canonical host configuration and never build security-sensitive URLs from unvalidated client headers.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Check reset emails, absolute links, multi-tenant routing
  • Headers: Host and forwarded-host variants
Sources: PortSwigger Host Header · Chrome DevTools Network

Description

This bug focuses on import/export feature review so you can verify whether This day is about all the extra steps after a file or document enters the system: parse, convert, store, preview, export, and notify. Data importers and exporters often mix parsing, trust, and background processing..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the upload, import, export, or attachment feature using your own test account.
  2. Upload or submit the file once normally and note each stage: validation, preview, storage, and download.
  3. Repeat the same flow with a file that sits near the allowed boundary in your authorized setup.
  4. Check whether the application trusts the file too much at any later stage like preview, conversion, or direct access.
  5. If the file flow breaks the expected boundary, save the stage, file type, and final server behavior.

Impact

The issue weakens application trust boundaries and should be documented with precise, reproducible evidence.

Mitigation

Tighten the backend trust boundary, add explicit server-side validation, and retest the smallest reproducible path after the fix.

Days 17-160 ke liye reproduce/process blocks ko aur simple, repo-style, step-by-step format me rewrite kiya gaya hai taaki practice flow easy lage.
Path traversal and local file access awareness
file-read

Description

This bug focuses on path traversal and local file access awareness so you can verify whether This day is about user-controlled file references and whether the application safely restricts local path access. User-controlled file references should be normalized, constrained, and authorized..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the download, document view, attachment, or template-based file path feature.
  2. Capture the normal request that fetches a valid file.
  3. Change only the file path, file name, or object reference in your authorized test setup.
  4. Forward the request and compare whether the server stays inside the intended file boundary.
  5. If another internal file becomes reachable, save the original request, changed value, and response difference.

Impact

Path-handling failures can disclose configuration files, secrets, or internal content outside the intended directory boundary.

Mitigation

Normalize paths, enforce allowlisted directories, separate storage identifiers from filesystem paths, and deny traversal outside the intended boundary.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Common surfaces: download, view, template, backup, attachment
  • Artifacts: requested path versus returned file
Sources: PortSwigger Path Traversal · OWASP WSTG
DAY 067 XML parser and XXE awareness Server-Side Trust Boundaries 1 bug block ▶
Phase: Server-Side Trust BoundariesResearch expansion dayHands-on reproduce block included

XML parser and XXE awareness
xml

Description

This bug focuses on xml parser and xxe awareness so you can verify whether This day is about XML-capable parsers and how unsafe parsing options can transform data handling into trust problems. Any XML-capable feature deserves parser-hardening and safe default review..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the XML upload, import, or API feature in your authorized lab or owned application.
  2. Submit a normal XML request first so you know the baseline response.
  3. Repeat the request while changing only the parser-relevant XML structure in a safe test case.
  4. Check whether the application behaves as if it trusted external XML processing more than it should.
  5. If the parser boundary is weak, save the request, response, and the exact XML feature that caused it.

Impact

Unsafe XML parsing can expose internal files, trigger outbound requests, or let untrusted content alter parser behavior.

Mitigation

Disable external entities, external DTD resolution, and unsafe parser features; validate XML inputs against the exact required format.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Common sinks: XML APIs, office docs, feeds, importers
  • Evidence: external fetch or file-boundary behavior
Sources: OWASP XXE Prevention · OWASP API Security
DAY 068 Template rendering safety Server-Side Trust Boundaries 1 bug block ▶
Phase: Server-Side Trust BoundariesResearch expansion dayHands-on reproduce block included
Days 17-160 ke liye reproduce/process blocks ko aur simple, repo-style, step-by-step format me rewrite kiya gaya hai taaki practice flow easy lage.
Template rendering safety
template

Description

This bug focuses on template rendering safety so you can verify whether This day is about server-side rendering engines and what happens when user-controlled data influences template logic. When user input reaches template engines, rendering logic can become execution logic..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the feature that stores names, messages, invites, or templates and later renders them on the server.
  2. Enter a harmless template-style test value in the user-controlled field.
  3. Submit the form and open the page, email, or preview where the value is rendered back.
  4. Compare whether the application prints your input as plain text or interprets it as template logic.
  5. If server-side rendering trusts the input too much, save the input field, rendered result, and affected template path.

Impact

Template injection can convert normal content fields into server-side logic execution or sensitive internal data exposure.

Mitigation

Render untrusted input as data, disable unsafe template capabilities, and separate user content from executable template expressions.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Common sinks: welcome emails, previews, names, invite text
  • Evidence: expression treated as logic instead of text
Sources: PortSwigger SSTI · PortSwigger All Labs
DAY 069 Unsafe command execution awareness Server-Side Trust Boundaries 1 bug block ▶
Phase: Server-Side Trust BoundariesResearch expansion dayHands-on reproduce block included
Days 17-160 ke liye reproduce/process blocks ko aur simple, repo-style, step-by-step format me rewrite kiya gaya hai taaki practice flow easy lage.
Unsafe command execution awareness
backend-exec

Description

This bug focuses on unsafe command execution awareness so you can verify whether This day is about applications that wrap system tools or background jobs and accidentally treat user input as commands. Learn to recognize when backend tools, jobs, or wrappers turn input into commands..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the diagnostic, conversion, logging, or backend-processed feature only in an official lab or your owned application.
  2. Submit the feature once normally and capture the exact request.
  3. Repeat the same request while changing only the user-controlled value that reaches the backend process.
  4. Watch for an observable backend-side behavior difference such as error pattern, output change, or unexpected processing.
  5. If the backend treats the input as trusted execution context, save the request pair and the smallest visible effect.

Impact

If input reaches backend command execution, the issue can quickly escalate from a single field to server compromise or sensitive data exposure.

Mitigation

Avoid shell invocation when possible, parameterize backend operations, allowlist inputs, and isolate risky utilities from untrusted data.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Common sinks: converters, admin tools, diagnostics
  • Record the smallest execution indicator
Sources: PortSwigger Command Injection · OWASP WSTG

Unsafe deserialization awareness
deserialization

Description

This bug focuses on unsafe deserialization awareness so you can verify whether This day is about object trust, parsing, and what happens when complex serialized data is accepted too easily. Serialized objects, signed blobs, and import formats all deserve trust review..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the feature that accepts serialized or structured state in your official lab or owned application.
  2. Capture the normal request, cookie, or body value first.
  3. Repeat the same action while changing only the serialized state in a safe, minimal way.
  4. Compare whether the server trusts the modified state more than it should.
  5. If the application accepts unsafe state changes through deserialization, save the original value, modified value, and response difference.

Impact

Unsafe deserialization can transform attacker-controlled state into server-side logic influence or code-path control.

Mitigation

Avoid unsafe native deserialization for untrusted input, sign or verify serialized state, and use safer structured formats where possible.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Artifacts: serialized blob, integrity guard, parser error or logic change
  • Prefer lab-safe demonstrations
Sources: PortSwigger Insecure Deserialization · PortSwigger All Labs
DAY 071 Cloud storage exposure and object ACLs Server-Side Trust Boundaries 1 bug block ▶
Phase: Server-Side Trust BoundariesResearch expansion dayHands-on reproduce block included

Cloud storage exposure and object ACLs
cloud-exposure

Description

This bug focuses on cloud storage exposure and object acls so you can verify whether This day is about storage permissions, object links, and how cloud exposure changes the effective security boundary. Buckets, object URLs, and signed links change how access control behaves..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the file, media, or report feature that uses cloud object storage or signed URLs.
  2. Open the generated object URL or signed link once normally.
  3. Reuse the same link later, from another browser, or after the expected access window should end.
  4. Compare whether the object still opens beyond the intended user, time, or session boundary.
  5. If the link remains valid too broadly or too long, save the URL pattern, expiry behavior, and exposed object type.

Impact

Object-store and signed-link issues can expose protected assets outside the UI’s intended access controls.

Mitigation

Tighten object ACLs, shorten signed-link lifetimes, bind them to the right object and user context, and keep storage listings private.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Artifacts: object URL, expiration, listing behavior, CDN cache
  • Compare application authz with direct object access
Sources: OWASP API Security · Chrome DevTools Network
DAY 072 Secrets in mobile/web clients Server-Side Trust Boundaries 1 bug block ▶

Secrets in mobile/web clients
source-exposure

Description

This bug focuses on secrets in mobile/web clients so you can verify whether This day is about what front-end code, mobile bundles, and shipped assets reveal about APIs, environments, or secrets. Client bundles, config files, and app metadata often reveal useful context or sensitive hints..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the public page, JavaScript file, debug route, mobile bundle, or client config related to the feature.
  2. Open DevTools Network tab and inspect the loaded assets one by one.
  3. Search the response bodies for hidden routes, keys, debug flags, source maps, or environment details.
  4. Compare whether the exposed data should really be visible to a normal user.
  5. If sensitive internals are disclosed, save the file path, redacted evidence, and the exposed context.

Impact

Client-side asset leaks can reduce attacker uncertainty by revealing routes, internal assumptions, or sensitive configuration details.

Mitigation

Remove secrets from shipped assets, restrict source-map publication, and keep client config intentionally minimal.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Artifacts: source maps, config JSON, shipped JS comments
  • Look for hidden APIs, roles, or environment names
Sources: Chrome DevTools Network · OWASP API Security
DAY 073 Default credentials and first-run setup risk Server-Side Trust Boundaries 1 bug block ▶
Phase: Server-Side Trust BoundariesResearch expansion dayHands-on reproduce block included

Default credentials and first-run setup risk
default-creds

Description

This bug focuses on default credentials and first-run setup risk so you can verify whether This day is about first-run paths, forgotten consoles, and setup defaults that remain more trusted than they should be. Setup paths and forgotten admin surfaces are security surfaces, not just ops details..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the exposed setup, admin, console, or device login page in your owned environment or official lab.
  2. Check whether the interface appears to be first-run or using vendor-default style access.
  3. Test only the documented default state needed for minimal proof.
  4. Stop after confirming whether the default access path is accepted.
  5. If default credentials or first-run trust still work, save the login page, product context, and acceptance proof without storing live secrets.

Impact

Default or unchanged setup credentials can hand administrative access to anyone who reaches the exposed interface.

Mitigation

Force credential rotation on first use, remove default accounts where possible, and protect setup paths from normal exposure.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Check first-run panels, appliances, test consoles
  • Record only the accepted default state, not real secrets
Sources: Default Credentials Ref · OWASP WSTG
DAY 074 Debug pages and verbose errors Server-Side Trust Boundaries 1 bug block ▶
Phase: Server-Side Trust BoundariesResearch expansion dayHands-on reproduce block included
Days 17-160 ke liye reproduce/process blocks ko aur simple, repo-style, step-by-step format me rewrite kiya gaya hai taaki practice flow easy lage.
Debug pages and verbose errors
info-disclosure

Description

This bug focuses on debug pages and verbose errors so you can verify whether This day is about extra detail in errors, diagnostics, and debug pages that removes uncertainty for the wrong person. Verbose diagnostics reduce uncertainty for attackers and confusion for defenders..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the public page, debug path, backup file, download, or client asset that is being reviewed.
  2. Open the response directly in the browser and also inspect it in DevTools or your proxy.
  3. Check whether it reveals credentials, internal paths, verbose errors, or other sensitive data.
  4. Redact any live secret immediately and keep only the minimum proof needed for reporting.
  5. If sensitive information is exposed, save the path, response type, and business impact.

Impact

Information disclosure reduces attacker guesswork and can expose secrets, debug context, credentials, or sensitive architecture clues.

Mitigation

Disable directory listings and verbose debug output, move secrets out of public artifacts, and sanitize what error paths reveal.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Artifacts: debug pages, backups, repo leaks, verbose errors
  • Always redact real secrets in notes and screenshots
Sources: PortSwigger Information Disclosure · Chrome DevTools Network

Front-end symptom vs back-end cause
file-flow

Description

This bug focuses on front-end symptom vs back-end cause so you can verify whether This day is about all the extra steps after a file or document enters the system: parse, convert, store, preview, export, and notify. Translate visible UI oddities into hypotheses about caches, parsers, jobs, or authz logic..

Reproduce / Process

  1. Go to the upload, import, export, or attachment feature using your own test account.
  2. Upload or submit the file once normally and note each stage: validation, preview, storage, and download.
  3. Repeat the same flow with a file that sits near the allowed boundary in your authorized setup.
  4. Check whether the application trusts the file too much at any later stage like preview, conversion, or direct access.
  5. If the file flow breaks the expected boundary, save the stage, file type, and final server behavior.

Impact

The issue weakens application trust boundaries and should be documented with precise, reproducible evidence.

Mitigation

Tighten the backend trust boundary, add explicit server-side validation, and retest the smallest reproducible path after the fix.

Evidence / Variants:
  • Focus: Front-end symptom vs back-end cause
  • Preserve the smallest reproducible proof with clear scope.
Sources: OWASP File Upload · PortSwigger File Upload
DAY 076 Scope reading as recon step zero Recon & Surface Mapping 1 bug block ▶
Phase: Recon & Surface MappingResearch expansion dayHands-on reproduce block included
